questions.statement: How did they get to the city center?
questions.context:
A description of a Saturday trip.
"On Saturday, we had breakfast early. Then, we took the bus to the city center. We bought some souvenirs and drank fresh orange juice."

options.feedback: Incorrect. This was before the trip.

questions.explanation:
The student applies reading skills to understand actions described with irregular past verbs.

questions.subject: ingles

questions.context: Identifying the correct combination of irregular verbs.

options.text: I make a cake and bring it to the party yesterday.
options.feedback: Incorrect. Both verbs should be in the past.

options.text: I maked a cake and brought it to the party yesterday.
options.feedback: Incorrect. "Make" is irregular, its past is "made".

options.text: I made a cake and brought it to the party yesterday.
options.feedback: Correct! "Made" and "brought" are the correct irregular past forms.

options.text: I made a cake and bringed it to the party yesterday.
options.feedback: Incorrect. "Bring" is irregular, its past is "brought".

questions.explanation:
The student analyzes multiple irregular verbs to ensure they are both correctly conjugated in the past tense.

questions.subject: ingles

questions.context:
Comparing past actions.
"Mateo told me a secret. Then, I spoke to Elena about it. She felt very surprised."

options.text: Mateo said something to the narrator.
options.feedback: Correct! "Told" is the past of "tell"; this was the first action.
Incorrect. The narrator spoke to Elena.
Incorrect. This was the final result.
Incorrect. Elena was the surprised one.

questions.explanation:
The student analyzes the sequence of events described using irregular past verbs (tell -> told, speak -> spoke, feel -> felt).

questions.subject: ingles

questions.statement: Which statement best evaluates Sara's performance and its result?
questions.context:
A summary of a student's past achievement.
"Sara did her best in the competition. She ran faster than ever and won the gold medal. She came home very happy and told her parents everything."

options.text: She didn't do much and lost the competition.
options.feedback: Incorrect. She won.

options.text: She was fast, but she didn't win anything.
options.feedback: Incorrect. She won the gold medal.

options.text: Her effort led to a victory and a shared celebration with her family.
options.feedback: Correct! "Did her best" and "ran faster" (effort) led to "won" (victory), and she "told her parents" (celebration).

options.text: She ran slowly and felt sad.
options.feedback: Incorrect. She ran "faster than ever".

questions.explanation: The student evaluates the logical connections between the past actions and outcomes described in the text.
